Force on a 2 kg particle varies with time as $\dot{F}=6 t \hat{i}-6 t^{2} \hat{j}$. Particle start from rest. Find power delivered by the force as a function of time.
(1) $9 t^{3}+4 t^{5}$
(2) $9 t^{3}+6 t^{5}$
(3) $6 t^{2}+3 t^{4}$
(4) $4 t^{2}+6 t^{3}$

steps:
$$\begin{array}{ll} 
& \dot{F}=6 t \hat{i}-6 t^{2} \hat{j} \\
\Rightarrow & \dot{a}=\frac{\dot{F}}{m}=3 t \hat{i}-3 t^{2} \hat{j} \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{d \dot{v}}{d t}=3 t \hat{i}-3 t^{2} \hat{j} \\
\Rightarrow & \int_{0}^{v} d \dot{v}=\frac{3 t^{2}}{2} \hat{i}-\left.t^{3}\right|_{0} ^{t} \quad(m=2 k g) \\
\Rightarrow & \dot{v}=\frac{3 t^{2}}{2} \hat{i}-t^{3} \hat{j} \\
\Rightarrow & P=\dot{F} \cdot \dot{v} \\
& P=\left(\left(6 t \hat{i}-6 t^{2} \hat{j}\right) \cdot\left(\frac{3 t^{2}}{2} \hat{i}-t^{3} \hat{j}\right)\right.
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
If in the given expression, $\mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{x}^{2}}{\mathrm{at}}$, where E represents energy, x represents length and t represents time Then, find dimension of $\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{b}}$.
(1) $\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-2} \mathrm{~T}$
(2) $\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-2} \mathrm{~T}^{-1}$
(3) $\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{-2} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}$
(4) $\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~T}$

steps:
$E=\frac{b}{a t}-\frac{x^{2}}{a t} \Rightarrow[E]=\left[\frac{b}{a t}\right]=\left[\frac{x^{2}}{a t}\right]$
$$\begin{array}{l}
{[\mathrm{E}]=\left[\frac{\mathrm{x}^{2}}{\mathrm{at}}\right] \Rightarrow\left[\mathrm{ML}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{2}\right]=\frac{\left[\mathrm{L}^{2}\right]}{[\mathrm{a}][\mathrm{T}]}} \\
\Rightarrow[\mathrm{a}]=\frac{\left[\mathrm{ML}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{2}\right][\mathrm{T}]}{\left[\mathrm{L}^{2}\right]}=\left[\mathrm{MT}^{1}\right] \\
\Rightarrow[\mathrm{E}]=\frac{[\mathrm{b}]}{\left.\mathrm{MT}^{-1}\right][\mathrm{T}]} \Rightarrow[\mathrm{b}]=\left[\mathrm{ML}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{2}\right]\left[\mathrm{MT}^{1}\right][\mathrm{T}] \\
{[\mathrm{b}]=\left[\mathrm{M}^{2} \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{2}\right]} \\
{\left[\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{~b}}\right]=\frac{\left[\mathrm{MT}^{1}\right]}{\left.\mathrm{M}^{2} \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{2}\right]}=\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~T}}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
Magnetic flux passing through a loop of resistance $8 \Omega$ is given by $\phi=5 t^{2}-3 t+5$. Find current in the loop at $\mathrm{t}=2$ second.
(1) 1.125 A
(2) 2.25 A
(3) 4.25 A
(4) 2.125 A

steps:
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon & =-\frac{d \phi}{d t} \\
& =-\frac{d}{d t}\left(5 t^{2}-3 t+5\right) \\
\varepsilon & =-(10 t-3) \\
\text { at } t & =2 \mathrm{sec} . \\
\varepsilon & =-(10 \times 2-3)=-17 \\
\mathrm{i} & =\frac{\varepsilon}{R}=\frac{17}{8} \text { Ampere } \\
\mathrm{i} & =2.125 \text { Ampere }
\end{aligned}$$

A point object is placed in air at 100 cm from a convex spherical refractive surface having radius of curvature 20 cm and refractive index on other side is $\mu=1.5$. Find image distance
(1) 75 cm
(2) 100 cm
(3) 200 cm
(4) 50 cm

steps:
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\mu_{2}}{V}-\frac{\mu_{1}}{u}=\frac{\mu_{2}-\mu_{1}}{R} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1.5}{V}-\frac{1}{(-100)}=\frac{1.5-1}{20} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1.5}{V}+\frac{1}{100}=\frac{1}{40} \Rightarrow \frac{1.5}{V}=\frac{1}{40}-\frac{1}{100} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1.5}{V}=\frac{5-2}{200} \Rightarrow \frac{1.5}{V}=\frac{3}{200} \\
\Rightarrow \quad V=\frac{200 \times 1.5}{3} \\
\Rightarrow \quad V=100 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{array}$$

Two vector of equal magnitude A are inclined at an angle $\theta$ with each other. Find the magnitude of resultant vector
(1) $2 \mathrm{~A} \cos \left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)$
(2) $2 \mathrm{~A} \sin \left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)$
(3) $2 \mathrm{~A} \cos \theta$
(4) $2 A \sin \theta$

steps:
$$\begin{aligned}
\mid \text { Resultant } \mid & =\sqrt{A^{2}+A^{2}+2 A^{2} \cos \theta} \\
= & \sqrt{2 A^{2}+2 A^{2} \cos \theta} \\
= & \sqrt{2} A \sqrt{1+\cos \theta} \\
= & 2 A \cos \left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text:
Length of a pendulum is 20 cm and error in its measurement is 2mm. If it completes 50 oscillations in 40 sec. and time was measured by a watch of resolution 1 sec. Find \% error in calculation of acceleration due to gravity
(1) $8 \%$
(2) 4 \%
(3) $2 \%$
(4) 6 \%

steps:
$T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\ell}{g}}$
$$\left[T=\frac{40}{50}=\frac{4}{5} s\right]$$
$\mathrm{g}=\frac{4 \pi^{2} \ell}{\mathrm{~T}^{2}}$
$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{g}} \times 100 \%=\frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell} \times 100 \%+2 \frac{\Delta \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{~T}} \times 100 \%$
$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{g}} \times 100 \%=\left(\frac{0.2}{20}\right) \times 100+2 \times \frac{1}{40} \times 100$
$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{g}} \times 100 \%=6 \%$

A nucleus has mass number $A_{1}$ and volume $V_{1}$. Another nucleus has mass number $A_{2}$ and volume $V_{2}$ If relation between mass number is $A_{2}=4 A_{1}$ then find $V_{2}$
(1) $2 \mathrm{~V}_{1}$
(2) $8 \mathrm{~V}_{1}$
(3) $4 \mathrm{~V}_{1}$
(4) $\mathrm{V}_{1}$

steps:
$\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{r}_{0}(\mathrm{~A})^{\frac{1}{3}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
V_{1}=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(r_{0}\left(A_{1}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^{3}=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(r_{0}\right)^{3} A_{1} \\
V_{2}=\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(r_{0}\left(A_{2} \frac{1}{3}\right)^{3}=\frac{4}{3} \pi r_{0}^{3} A_{2}\right. \\
A_{2}=4 A_{1} \text { (given) } \\
V_{2}=\frac{4}{3} \pi r_{0}^{3}\left(4 A_{1}\right)=4 V_{1} \\
V_{2}=4 V_{1}
\end{array}$$

24. 1 mole of an ideal gas expands from 10 lit to 100 lit isothermally and reversibly at 300 K , then magnitude of work done is $\_\_\_\_$ (in kJ ) [Nearest integer]
[Given $\mathrm{R}=8.314 \frac{\mathrm{~J}}{\text { Mole × K }}$ ]

Ans. (6)
Sol. For isothermal reversible process
$$\begin{aligned}
W & =-n R T \ln \left(\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}\right) \\
& =-[1 \times 8.314 \times 300] 2.303 \log \left(\frac{100}{10}\right) \\
& =-2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \\
& =-5744 \mathrm{~J} \\
& =-5.744 \mathrm{~kJ}
\end{aligned}$$
